newsitem.title: GERMANY: GEA sees 96 net profit slightly under 95.
newsitem.headline: GEA sees 96 net profit slightly under 95.

text.p: German process technology supplier GEA AG said on Wednesday it expected 1996 net profit to fall just below the 1995 level of 111 million marks.
Previously the company had said it expected net profit to fall 10 percent below the 1995 figure, but revised its outlook since completing a reorganisation in November.
Closing some unprofitable operations and reducing debt to 400 million marks from 515 million marks allowed GEA to raise its profit forecast, the company said in a statement.
GEA also said chief executive Otto Happel would step down at the June 27 annual meeting and would be replaced by finance head Klaus Sturany. Happel would become chairman of GEA's supervisory board.

GEA said its slimmer organisation had resulted in a holding company that coordinates the activities of nine operating units with their own management boards, responsible for profit and loss. It eliminated a layer of administration and reduced the GEA holding company board to three members.
The number of employees at the end of 1996 fell to 17,833, down four percent from a year before.
